entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Papulus, a Christian priest, played a crucial role in evangelizing southern Gaul during the 4th century CE. 

Born in unknown circumstances, Papulus worked closely with Saturninus of Toulouse to spread Christianity to the region. 

Through their efforts, Papulus is considered an evangelist of the Lauragais, a significant region in modern-day France. 

Papulus's legacy extends beyond his immediate region, as Christianity continued to spread throughout Gaul and eventually across Europe. 

This legacy was cemented by the construction of numerous churches and monasteries, which became centers of learning and faith.

In the words of Saint Augustine, 'The City of God' was 'built upon the foundation of the Gospel of Christ', a testament to Papulus's enduring impact on Western civilization.

Despite the passing of centuries, Papulus's contributions to the Christian faith remain an essential part of its history and development.
